text: Withdrawals are capped at a daily limit of 5000.00 per account, which the plan never mentioned.
The daily withdrawal total is never reset, so the 'daily' limit is really a lifetime limit for the ledger instance.
The daily limit counts only the withdrawn amount, not the fee.
The withdrawal fee is capped at a maximum of 25.00.
The 1% withdrawal fee is rounded up to the next cent.
The fee is added to the withdrawal and recorded as one combined history entry instead of its own separate entry.
A withdrawal is rejected unless the balance covers both the amount and the fee, so no overdraft is allowed.
Transfers and split payments are rejected when the sender's balance would go negative.
Insufficient funds is checked before the daily limit, which decides which rejection reason the customer sees.
A repeated transaction id returns success without doing anything and without checking that the account, amount or type match the original.
Transaction ids are unique across the whole ledger, not per account or per operation type.
Input validation runs before the duplicate check, so a retry with a bad amount is rejected even if the txn id was already processed.
Rejected operations do not record their transaction id, so the same id can later succeed.
Accounts are created automatically on any operation, including withdrawals, transfers and splits that then fail.
Asking for the balance of an unknown account returns 0 rather than an error.
A transfer from an account to itself is accepted instead of rejected.
Foreign-currency deposits are rounded half away from zero instead of half to even.
The foreign amount is multiplied by the rate (rate means account currency per foreign unit).
A foreign deposit that converts to less than one cent is rejected as 'amount-too-small'.
Foreign deposits are recorded as plain 'deposit' entries with no currency or rate kept.
A regular deposit, withdrawal or transfer smaller than half a cent rounds to zero and is still accepted and recorded.
Infinity and arbitrarily large amounts pass the positive-number check.
A small epsilon is added before rounding amounts to cents to absorb floating-point error.
The interest rate is given as a percentage (5 means 5%), not a fraction.
Interest is simple (not compounded) over the given days.
Interest is rounded down to the cent.
When interest rounds to zero, or the balance is zero or negative, the call returns success with no entry and the transaction id is not recorded.
A zero or negative interest rate or day count is rejected, and fractional days are allowed.
In a split payment, leftover cents go one each to the first recipients in list order.
A split with no recipients is rejected.
Split recipients may repeat or include the payer.
Split payments charge no fee, and neither do transfers.
History amounts are stored as positive numbers for both credits and debits, so the direction comes only from the entry kind.
The rejection reason strings returned to callers are 'invalid-amount', 'amount-too-small', 'insufficient-funds', 'daily-limit' and 'no-recipients'.
